plants.name: Lycoris radiata
plants.description: Leafless stalks shoot up from the bare ground, each topped with a crown of crimson flowers. The petals curl back and the long stamens arch outward like delicate spider legs. In Japan, whole rice-field banks and village paths turn scarlet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-September to early October, peaking around the autumn equinox
plants.location: Japan, in rice-field margins, riverbanks and temple grounds across Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu
plants.funFact: The Japanese name Higanbana refers to Higan, the equinox week. The flowers appear so reliably then that they are used as a natural calendar for the autumn equinox. The leaves only emerge after the flowers fade.

plants.name: Sternbergia lutea
plants.description: Glossy golden goblets that look like crocuses sit low to the ground. They light up dry, rocky hillsides just as the summer drought breaks. Each bloom is cupped and waxy, and it opens wide in sunshine.
plants.bloomingSeason: September to November, usually starting in September
plants.location: Mediterranean region eastward to Central Asia, including Greece, Turkey and Spain, on dry stony slopes and olive groves
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, it is not a true crocus. It belongs to the amaryllis family. Many botanists suspect it is the 'lily of the field' mentioned in ancient texts.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Whole trees become clouds of fragrant, fluffy golden pompoms. Each ball is made up of 40 to 80 tiny flowers. The blossoms glow against the grey-green foliage and fill the bush with a honey-sweet scent.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring, with peak flowering from late August through September in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, New South Wales and Tasmania, in woodlands and open forests
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. Its green and gold colors inspired the country's national sporting colors. Australia also marks National Wattle Day on September 1.
